title: Adaptive mediator for balancing latency and throughput across prefill and decode phases
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Background: Current prefill/decode arbitration can cause tail latency spikes when long prefill work items collide with latency-sensitive decode requests. Kernel choices (fused attention vs. tiled attention) and attention-cost patterns across tokens make worst-case latencies hard to bound. Goal: build a lightweight 'mediator' scheduling policy that bridges kernel-selection signals and phase-splitting decisions to improve P95/P99 latency for latency-sensitive routes while preserving overall throughput and unit cost for bulk workloads.

What we're proposing: the mediator observes per-request kernel hints (estimated attention FLOP cost, sequence-length distribution, recommended kernel family) and runtime queue states, then: (1) computes a short-term latency headroom budget per latency-class, (2) decides whether to split an incoming prefill into micro-phases (micro-prefills) to free slots for pending decodes, (3) tags micro-phases with fairness weights (token-cost-weighted) so bulk workloads still get proportional service, and (4) emits kernel-probe hints to the kernel-selector so fused kernels are preferred for micro-prefills when beneficial. The mediator is policy-configurable (latency-weight, fairness-factor, max-micro-slices) and exposes a trace per-request for debugging.

Key design trade-offs: 
- Aggressively splitting reduces tail latency but increases kernel-switching overhead (more small kernels) and may fragment KV cache/compaction benefits.
- Conservative splitting preserves throughput but fails to protect latency-sensitive callers.
- Kernel probe frequency must be limited to avoid overhead; we use lightweight sampling + cached decisions per model-version.

Success criteria (measurable): 
- Reduce P95 latency for latency-sensitive label routes by >= 25% at 95th percentile load compared to current baseline.
- Keep throughput loss < 5% for bulk throughput jobs (measured over steady-state 15m windows).
- Unit token cost change within +/- 8% for typical workloads.

Rollout plan: 
1) Lab microbenchmarks: synthetic mixes (80/20 bulk/low-latency) measuring per-kernel latency and kernel-switch overhead.
2) Canary in Dedicated: enable mediator on single shard with traffic split (2% traffic) on runtime-1.21, monitor latency dashboards and error budgets.
3) Gradual ramp if metrics OK, else revert and iterate.

Rollback criteria: any sustained P99 increase > 15% for latency routes, or throughput regression > 10% for 10m window.

Observability: expose mediator metrics: micro-slices/sec, average slice size tokens, kernel-switches/sec, queued-decode-waits, fairness-violation-rate. Hook these into the Console per-route dashboard and alerts.

Open questions: how to parameterize fairness weight relative to customer tier (free vs paid)? Should kernel-probe be model-version or compilation fingerprint keyed? We'll prototype with model-version then consider fingerprinting in a follow-up.
